newsitem.title: EGYPT: Local firms beat foreigners for Egyptian oil blocks.
newsitem.headline: Local firms beat foreigners for Egyptian oil blocks.

text.p: Egypt has awarded oil exploration concessions to two local private-sector companies, both of which made better offers than their foreign rivals, the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) said on Sunday.

Abu El-Fouttouh, a company led by prominent Egyptian businessman Hossam Abu El-Fouttouh, won the Central Sinai block, an onshore area of 18,150 square km (7,010 square miles), said Wafik Meshref, EGPC vice president for agreements.
It beat off competition from Apache of the United States and the British-based company LK Exploration, he said.

Another Egyptian company, Eatco (Egyptian Arab Trading), chaired by Yahia el-Komi, won the North Gharib concession, an offshore block of 712 square km (275 square miles) in the Gulf of Suez, Meshref told Reuters. Eatco's rival for the award was Pennzoil of the United States.
Eatco is a newcomer to oil exploration in Egypt, while Abu El-Fouttouh was awarded the West Bahariya block last October.

The conditions for the Central Sinai block are that Abu El-Fouttouh must invest $6 million during an initial phase of three years, complete 500 km of two-dimensional seismic and 200 square km of three-dimensional seismic, drill four wells and pay a signature bonus of $1 million, he said.
For the North Gharib block, Eatco must spend $16 million over an initial phase of three years, drill four wells and pay a signature bonus of $800,000.
If the companies find oil in commercial quantities, they can take 35 percent of it for the first four years to recover their costs, Meshref added.
The EGPC bid committee will meet again later this month to look at three bids for the West Beni Suef block, which covers 38,000 square km (14,700 square miles) west of the Nile valley.
The bids, which arrived after the deadline expired last year, are from Apache, Global Natural Resources and Pennzoil, he said.
"We found the bids very close so we asked them to resubmit their bids by January 15 and then it will take about a week to look at them," he added.
Apache and Global Natural Resources are 50-50 partners in the adjacent East Beni Suef concession, with Global Natural Resources as operator, he said.
